title: Colimit formula in a coherent coslice and filtered constant diagrams
statement:
Use universes, accessibility and regular cardinals as in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent functor categories, weak contractibility, mapping spaces and colimits as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory admitting all small colimits, $X\in\mathcal C$, and $K$ a small simplicial set, possibly empty. Model the coherent coslice by $\mathcal C_{X/}:=\{X\}\times_{\mathcal C,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$. A diagram $q:K\to\mathcal C_{X/}$ is a coherent transformation $\alpha:\Delta_KX\to Y$, where $Y:K\to\mathcal C$. Put $A=\operatorname{colim}_K\Delta_KX$, $B=\operatorname{colim}_K Y$, let $a:A\to X$ be induced by the identity constant cocone, and let $b:A\to B$ be induced by $\alpha$. The arrow $X\to X\amalg_A B$, with the coherent cocone induced by the colimit cocones and the pushout square, is a colimit of $q$ in $\mathcal C_{X/}$.

If $K$ is weakly contractible, $a:A\to X$ is an equivalence. Every small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory is weakly contractible for every infinite regular $\kappa$. Consequently the functor $*\to\mathcal C$ with value $X$, where $*$ is the terminal quasicategory, preserves all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits; the terminal quasicategory is accessible.

source.place: Agent-formulated general coslice pushout formula from HTT Proposition 4.4.2.2, the coslice mapping-space fiber identification of Lemma 5.5.5.12, and the coherent mapping-space universal properties; weakly contractible constant diagrams: Proposition 4.3.1.12 over a point. Filtered weak contractibility checked in Kerodon Proposition 9.1.1.17, Tag 02PH (https://kerodon.net/tag/02PH); this is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag. Read online; no archived source or matching Stacks theorem.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ and $c=\Delta_KX$. The pointwise colimit theorem applied to the arrow diagram $\alpha$ gives $b:A\to B$, together with the compatible colimit cocones. Thus $b$ is induced by $\alpha$, rather than an unrelated arrow between its endpoint colimits. The identity cocone on $c$ gives $a:A\to X$. Choose the pushout $P=X\amalg_A B$, with structure maps $u:X\to P$ and $v:B\to P$ and its specified homotopy $ua\simeq vb$. The cocone $Y\to\Delta_KB\to\Delta_KP$ and this homotopy give a coherent cocone $\tau:q\to\Delta_Ku$ in the coslice: its common-source compatibility is the composite of the colimit compatibility for $\alpha$ with the pushout homotopy. All three colimits exist by the hypothesis on $\mathcal C$. For the mapping-space tests below one may work in a larger universe containing the mapping spaces of $\mathcal C$; no extra local-smallness hypothesis or additional colimits of $\mathcal C$ are used.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.2.2 (objectwise colimits); Proposition 4.4.2.2 and Remark 4.4.2.3 (induced maps and pushouts); agent construction of the coslice cocone

proof.text:
Fix $z:X\to Z$. In simplicial degree $n$, both $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C_{X/})$ and $\mathcal D_{c/}$ consist of maps $K\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$ whose source restriction is constant at $X$. Reordering product factors identifies these simplicial sets, including every operator; the constant diagram with value $z$ corresponds to $\Delta_Kz:c\to\Delta_KZ$. The coslice of an object $c$ in any quasicategory is precisely its cocone category for the one-point diagram with value $c$. Consequently the dual cone mapping-space formula, applied in $\mathcal D$ to that one-point diagram, gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C_{X/})}(q,\Delta_Kz)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_Kz}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Y,\Delta_KZ)\xrightarrow{\alpha^*}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(c,\Delta_KZ)\bigr).$$
The same formula in $\mathcal C$ identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{X/}}(u,z)$ with the fiber over $z$ of $u^*:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(P,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(X,Z)$. The cone-calculus theorem also ensures that the coslices and the functor categories used here are quasicategories and all these mapping spaces are Kan complexes.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.5.12; agent application to the one-point cocone category, both in C and in Fun(K,C)

proof.text:
The colimit cone criterion applied to $Y\to\Delta_KB$ and $c\to\Delta_KA$ gives natural equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Y,\Delta_KZ)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(B,Z),\qquad \operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(c,\Delta_KZ)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(A,Z).$$
Their naturality in $\alpha$ identifies $\alpha^*$ with $b^*$ and sends $\Delta_Kz$ to $za$: this follows by restricting to the colimit cocone components, since the identity cocone induces $a$. Homotopy-pullback invariance therefore identifies the first fiber in step 2 with $\operatorname{hofib}_{za}(b^*)$. Contravariant representables take the pushout defining $P$ to the homotopy pullback
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(P,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(X,Z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(A,Z)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(B,Z).$$
Its fiber over $z$ is $\operatorname{hofib}_{za}(b^*)$: on either side the data are $h:B\to Z$ and a path $hb\simeq za$, with all higher simplices. This is just iterated homotopy pullback, with the fixed point $z$ substituted in the first coordinate. These identifications are induced by $\tau$: a morphism $r:P\to Z$ with $ru\simeq z$ is sent to $rv$ with the path $rvb\simeq rua\simeq za$. Hence the actual comparison
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{X/}}(u,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C_{X/})}(q,\Delta_Kz)$$
is an equivalence, naturally in $z$. The dual cone criterion now proves that $\tau$ is colimiting. For $K=\varnothing$, $A$ and $B$ are initial, so the same pushout is equivalent to $X$ and $u$ to its identity; the argument never assumes that $K$ has a vertex.

source.place: Lemmas 5.5.5.12-5.5.5.13; Proposition 4.4.2.2; explicit comparison of the homotopy fibers, using the coherent cocone criterion

proof.text:
Suppose $K\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The groupoid-localization theorem identifies $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathcal C)$ with the full subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(K,\mathcal C)$. In particular for any $X,Z$, fullness and equivalence on mapping spaces show that the specific constant-transformation map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(X,Z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(\Delta_KX,\Delta_KZ)$$
is an equivalence. The dual cone criterion says exactly that the identity constant cocone with apex $X$ is colimiting. This argument proves existence of this particular colimit in any quasicategory, without assuming other colimits. Comparing it with the cocone defining $A$, the induced map is precisely $a:A\to X$. Both cocones are initial in the cocone category; their comparison maps are inverse up to homotopy since the relevant mapping spaces are contractible. Evaluation at the apex makes $a$ an equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.12 over a point; explicit full-mapping-space argument using the localization of K at all edges

proof.text: For use with the compact-support theorem, the finite cube $[0,1]^n$ is compact Hausdorff. Here is a reduction to the cited compact-simplex statement, avoiding an uncited compactness theorem. For $n\geq1$ the continuous map from the simplex on the $2^n$ vertices $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}^n$ to $[0,1]^n$ sends weights $(t_\epsilon)$ to $\sum_\epsilon t_\epsilon\epsilon$. It is surjective: for $x\in[0,1]^n$ use the nonnegative weights $t_\epsilon=\prod_{\epsilon_i=1}x_i\prod_{\epsilon_i=0}(1-x_i)$, whose sum is $1$ and whose weighted coordinate sums are $x_i$. The image is compact by pulling an open cover back to the compact simplex, taking a finite subcover and using surjectivity. It is Hausdorff since two unequal points have an unequal coordinate and disjoint coordinate intervals. For $n=0$ it is a point. Finite discrete spaces are likewise compact Hausdorff by choosing one cover member per point.

source.place: Agent finite convex-combination argument from the compactness of standard simplices (existing Mathlib leaf)

proof.text: Let $I$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory, with $\kappa$ infinite regular. Applying filteredness to the empty diagram gives a vertex. Any finite simplicial subset $F\subseteq I$ is $\kappa$-small, so its inclusion admits a coherent cocone $H_F:F\times\Delta^1\to I$ from that inclusion to a constant diagram at a vertex $i_F$. By the realization-cylinder theorem, $|H_F|\rho_F^{-1}$ is a continuous homotopy from the realized inclusion $e_F:|F|\to|I|$ to the constant map at $i_F$. For any two points of $|I|$, apply compact finite support to the map from a two-point discrete space. Both points factor through a single finite $F$; the two tracks of this homotopy give paths to $i_F$. Thus $|I|$ is nonempty and path connected. This uses actual coherent cocones, not just cones in the ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: Proposition 9.1.1.17 and Remark 9.1.1.14; agent realization version using compact finite support instead of Kan replacement

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ let $f:([0,1]^n,\partial[0,1]^n)\to(|I|,x)$ represent any homotopy-group element. By step 5 and compact finite support, $f=e_Ff_F$ for a continuous $f_F:[0,1]^n\to|F|$ and finite $F\subseteq I$. The realization inclusion is a homeomorphism onto its image by the simplicial-subcomplex theorem, hence is injective. Since $f$ is constant at $x$ on the boundary, $f_F$ is constant on the boundary at a point $x_F$ with $e_F(x_F)=x$. Apply the homotopy of step 6 to $e_F$. The basepoint-change theorem gives $(e_F)_*=\beta_\gamma\circ(\operatorname{const}_{i_F})_*$ on $\pi_n(|F|,x_F)$, where $\gamma$ is the track of $x_F$. The latter induced map is zero, since every composite is constant. Thus $[f]=(e_F)_*[f_F]=0$. This treats moving basepoints correctly, without asserting that the cocone homotopy fixes $x$. Together with the path-component calculation in step 6, all the groups and components in the definition of weak contractibility show that $I\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Only finite diagrams were needed, so the argument applies to every infinite regular $\kappa$, including $\aleph_0$.

source.place: Proposition 9.1.1.17; agent compact-support and basepoint-change expansion of its nullhomotopy argument

proof.text: The terminal quasicategory $*$ has one simplex in each degree. Every $I$-diagram in it and its cocone category are terminal simplicial sets, so its unique cocone is colimiting. Its image under the functor selecting $X$ is the identity constant cocone. For $I$ small $\kappa$-filtered, steps 6-7 make $I$ weakly contractible and step 4 makes that image cocone colimiting. This proves preservation for each infinite regular $\kappa$. Finally $*$ is locally small and admits these colimits. Its sole object $e$ is $\kappa$-compact: $\operatorname{Map}_*(e,e)=\Delta^0$, and for every such $I$, step 4 applied to the quasicategory of spaces says that the colimit of the constant point diagram is the point, so its comparison with $\operatorname{Map}_*(e,\operatorname{colim}_I e)$ is an equivalence. The one-object full subcategory is small and generates $e$ by the singleton diagram. Its indexing category $\Delta^0$ is $\kappa$-filtered, since every diagram into it has a unique coherent cocone. These are all the clauses of $\kappa$-accessibility in the cited definition, so $*$ is accessible.

source.place: Definition 5.5.0.1 and accessibility/compactness conventions; agent verification using the preceding constant-diagram and filtered-contractibility steps
